questions.q: Which column does this lesson identify as the one that must always be a named individual, never a team or department?
options: Likelihood
Owner
Status
Risk ID
questions.explain: Owner must be a specific, named person accountable for the risk's resolution — naming a team lets accountability diffuse to nobody.

questions.q: Why does R-04 stay in the register marked "Mitigated" instead of being deleted once the automation's failure alert is in place?
options: Because deleting rows is technically impossible in most GRC tools
Because a register has to keep showing what was identified and what was done about it, so anyone can later confirm the control is still effective
Because Howard Okonjo requires every row to stay forever regardless of status
Because R-04 has not actually been fixed yet
questions.explain: A risk register tracks the full lifecycle of a risk, including mitigated ones, so it can answer whether a control is still working later -- not just what was found.

questions.q: What does R-03 specifically identify as the structural weakness in Hartwell's break-glass emergency-access procedure?
options: That break-glass access requires too many approvals to use quickly
That it has no automatic expiration, so elevated access stays active until someone manually revokes it
That it only works for Azure AD accounts, not AWS IAM accounts
That it is not documented anywhere
questions.explain: R-03 names exactly this: break-glass grants don't expire on their own, so the compensating control is a manual 72-hour follow-up ticket -- a control that depends on someone remembering to act.

questions.q: What does R-05 schedule, and why does it matter heading into the next lesson?
options: A penetration test of the OT/SCADA segment
A quarterly compliance audit of standing access to Critical-tier segments like OT/SCADA -- which is exactly what starts in Lesson 11
A full rebuild of the risk register from scratch
A vendor contract renewal
questions.explain: R-05 directly sets up the compliance audit that Lesson 11 covers -- the register isn't just background, it's the reason the audit is about to happen at all.

questions.q: What is a "compensating control" in this register, as distinct from the Treatment column?
options: A second, unrelated risk logged alongside the first
What's actually in place right now to reduce the risk while the permanent fix is still being implemented
The person who approved the Treatment decision
A synonym for "Status"
questions.explain: Treatment is the overall decision (accept/mitigate/transfer/avoid); the compensating control is the concrete, present-tense interim measure reducing exposure while the full fix is still in progress.
